Thanks for the intro — excited to get Redwood live for PayZon. We're getting our engineering team aligned for the integration sprint and wanted a consolidated plan for SDK setup, endpoint migration (we currently use an in-house endpoint), and your recommendations for retries/timeouts and rate-limit behavior.

A few specifics from our side:
- Peak burst: ~400 rps sustained for short bursts; average 60 rps during business hours.
- Current client stack: Node 18 + a small Go microservice for async jobs.
- Compliance need: log retention proof for the first 30 days of traffic.

What would be most helpful: a short implementation checklist, a minimal example in Node and Python, and the expected headers/behavior on 429s and transient 5xxs. Also, can we get a draft runbook we can review before our kickoff?

Planning to propose a 45-minute technical kickoff for next week — what times work for your team?

Alex — attaching the SDK samples (payzon_sdk_samples.zip) and an abbreviated migration checklist below so your engs can read immediately. The zip contains Node and Python examples and a Postman collection for quick smoke tests.

Abbreviated migration checklist (technical):
- Create sandbox API key (we've provisioned one for PayZon).
- Run smoke test: POST /v1/generate -> 5 sample prompts (see Postman).
- Confirm tokenization and max-seq settings in your caller to avoid unexpected truncation.
- Implement retry and timeout as described below.
- Schedule a 2-hour canary during off-peak.
- Monitor: token-level latency and error-rate dashboards; hold cutover if 429 > 1% sustained for 5m.

Minimal sample (Python) — recommended client config:

import time
from redwood import RedwoodClient, RetryPolicy

client = RedwoodClient(api_key="sk-sandbox-payzon-001", endpoint="https://api.redwood.ai/v1", timeout=10)
# Retry: exponential backoff with jitter, 5 attempts max
client.retry_policy = RetryPolicy(max_attempts=5, base_delay=0.25, max_delay=8.0, jitter=True, retry_on=[429, 502, 503, 504])

resp = client.generate("Summarize transaction batch #42")
print(resp.text)

Notes on timeouts: we recommend a per-request timeout of 8–12s for sync generation calls and an HTTP connection timeout of 2s. For streaming, ensure the client keeps the socket open for at least 60s of inactivity.

Rate-limit guidance (short):
- Default hosted tier: 120 rps with 10 concurrent streams.
- For bursts, we recommend a soft-burst policy + token bucket throttling on client side.
- PayZon is in scope for autoscale; we'll propose Dedicated capacity or reserved burst tokens in the quote.

Attachments: payzon_sdk_samples.zip (Node + Python + Postman collection)

Happy to walk through the code during the kickoff.

Alex — answers inline and a few explicit recommendations.

On 2026-10-14 Alex wrote:
> If a 429 occurs, do you return a Retry-After header or a body payload with recommended delay?

We return standard HTTP 429 with the Retry-After header (seconds) on Hosted endpoints. For Dedicated customers we can surface X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset headers on request/response for tighter client-side enforcement. Our hosted pattern: 429 + Retry-After (seconds) + body with short guidance. Example:

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 12
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "retry_seconds": 12
}

Recommendation: implement exponential backoff with full jitter and honor Retry-After when present. Suggested pseudo-policy: base=0.25s, factor=2, max_attempts=6, max_delay=20s.

> For streaming responses, how do you recommend handling partial results if a connection is dropped mid-stream? Any guidance on idempotency or resume?

Streaming resume: currently we do not support stream resume across network disconnects for generation streams. Two patterns:
- Buffering client-side: client consumes partial stream and on disconnect re-issues a shorter prompt containing the last N tokens as context to continue.
- Checkpointing via server-side: for large async jobs use our async Jobs API which writes strong state and can be polled for completion; this path supports idempotent job IDs and retries.

> Can you confirm the SSO/SAML flows for our sandbox -> prod migration?

Yes — we support Okta with SAML 2.0. Grace will share our SSO setup doc and a temporary test assertion consumer URL for sandbox. For prod, we'll exchange metadata XML and coordinate certificate rotation windows.

Implementation checklist (short, actionable):
- Use SDK samples in payzon_sdk_samples.zip to run smoke tests in sandbox.
- Set client retry_policy as recommended and honor Retry-After.
- For burst protection: implement a local token-bucket limiter with capacity tuned to your peak burst (we can propose values in the kickoff).
- Add observability hooks: measure 429 rate, 5xx rate, median token latency; alert on 429 > 1% sustained over 5m.
- Cutover plan: 10% canary for 30m -> 25% for 30m -> 100% if stable. Rollback if 5xx or 429 exceed thresholds.

Meeting: we've booked a 45-minute kickoff for Oct 14 at 11:00 PT and sent calendar invite to Alex and team. Monica will demo the Node sample; I'll walk the canary plan and the rate-limit header behavior.

Attachments: integration_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook), payzon_sdk_samples.zip (samples)

See you on the call — Vivek
